summary: Encinitas stretches across six miles of coastline along sandstone bluffs that rise 50 to 100 feet above the Pacific, and from certain vantage points along the cliff-edge trails you can watch both surfers below and, on clear days, Catalina Island roughly 70 miles offshore — a geographic peculiarity that even some long-time San Diego County residents don't realize. The city's 20 square miles roll inland through a mix of coastal mesa, flower-growing greenhouses (Encinitas was once the poinsettia capital of the world, and commercial horticulture still marks the landscape), and the lagoon ecosystems of San Elijo and Batiquitos, both of which offer flat, well-maintained trail loops right at sea level. Highway 101 threads through the original downtown corridor with an unusual density of independent restaurants, surf shops, and cafés that give the strip a texture distinctly its own, while Interstate 5 bisects the city and creates a real east-west divide — neighborhoods west of the freeway have walkable beach access, while eastern areas around the Olivenhain community feel semi-rural with equestrian lots and canyon edges. With a median home value near $1.47 million against a median household income of about $150,000, the price-to-income ratio sits close to 9.7, meaning even at the local median income a conventional mortgage stretches well past standard affordability thresholds; median rent at $2,730 consumes roughly 22% of that same gross income, a notably less painful ratio. The Coaster commuter rail stops in downtown Encinitas and connects to central San Diego in about 50 minutes, but the city itself is not a major employment hub — biotech and healthcare clusters in nearby Carlsbad, Sorrento Valley, and La Jolla pull many commuters south along I-5's notoriously congested corridor. Daily highs averaging 70°F year-round with nearly nine hours of sunshine per day mean the mild, dry climate barely fluctuates between seasons, which makes the outdoor infrastructure — bluff-top paths, lagoon trails, the San Elijo State Beach campground — functional twelve months a year rather than seasonal. Encinitas is a place where the Pacific Ocean is genuinely part of the daily built environment rather than a weekend destination, but that proximity is capitalized into every square foot of housing cost.
